Job preference in coal development positions for Crow Indians is a part of present mining operations. It is anticipated that this will continue to be an integral part of future agreements.
Economic Impacts
From an economic viewpoint, the most important mitigating factor is the income generated by coal development. Royalties to the tribe, employment and business income related to coal development and associated services, and the direct and indirect tax revenues these produce will make possible the funding of programs essential to an orderly, functioning community. These important economic aspects have been fully analyzed and presented in Chapter III.
The effectiveness of these mitigating measures will depend on the people of the area and their ability to plan and implement programs which, will provide the necessary community services, land use controls, and administrative structures.
Services Impacts
Increased Health Services - will be an obvious need associated with a high level of coal development. These services will call for a significant increases in capital investment and operational cost.
There are a number of programs available which will have a mitigating effect. The most comprehensive one is the Partnership for Health Program (Public Health Service Act Title III as amended) of Health, Education and Welfare.
